# Part II: Data and Learning Systems {.unnumbered}

With the physical container, physical limits, and arbitration hardware established in Part I, Part II focuses on how the machine acquires the capacity to act. Where Part I derived the physical constraints of the body and nervous system, Part II tackles the data collection, training systems, and evaluation pipelines required to build robust embodied models.

In disembodied machine learning, models are trained on static, independently distributed datasets where errors manifest as classification errors or text hallucinations. In Physical AI, the data distribution is endogenous: every action taken by the policy alters the state of the physical plant, directly dictating what the sensors observe next. A small tracking error compounds dynamically ($O(T^2 \epsilon)$), driving the machine into out-of-distribution physical states. Part II teaches engineers how to collect multi-modal demonstration data, train continuous action-chunking policies, and evaluate closed-loop physical deployments.

### The Pillars of Part II

Part II develops the lifecycle of physical learning systems across three foundational chapters:

* **Chapter 5: Data Systems (*Collection, Teleoperation & Ingestion Pipelines*):** Analyzes the physical origins of robotic datasets, comparing leader-follower teleoperation, kinesthetic teaching, and autonomous collection. Quantifies multi-camera timestamp synchronization, proprioceptive sensor drift, and Open X-Embodiment dataset schemas.
* **Chapter 6: Training Systems (*Imitation Learning, Diffusion Policies & Sim-to-Real*):** Details how to train continuous control policies, analyzing behavioral cloning, Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT), Diffusion Policies, and reinforcement learning. Examines physics simulators as systems components and decomposes the sim-to-real gap into contact friction, backlash, and actuator phase lag.
* **Chapter 7: Evaluation Systems (*Closed-Loop Benchmarking & Physical Failure Modes*):** Formulates the systems boundaries of offline validation versus closed-loop physical rollouts. Proves why open-loop test loss is decoupled from physical task success, constructs selective execution curves, and establishes statistical bounds on physical reliability.

### What You Will Master in Part II

By the conclusion of Part II, you will be equipped to build end-to-end data and training pipelines for physical machines:

1. **Handling Compounding Errors:** Overcoming the $O(T^2 \epsilon)$ compounding covariate shift in behavioral cloning through recovery demonstration logging and action chunking.
2. **Bridging the Sim-to-Real Gap:** Sizing domain randomization budgets and system identification parameters to transfer policies from simulation to physical hardware.
3. **Closed-Loop Evaluation:** Designing standardized physical benchmarking protocols that measure true task completion, cycle times, intervention rates, and worst-case failure modes.
